payload.review:
DEPENDENCIES, displayed in full with their standing rulings; no new ask is owed to the owner.

RUNTIME npm dependencies: NONE, unchanged - the count is still zero, and this iteration deliberately kept it there. The crypto rides node:crypto plus the platform's Web Crypto (globalThis.crypto.subtle, which is also exactly what the browser runs, so one implementation serves both sides); the store rides fetch. Nothing was added to package.json. This honours the owner's standing ruling that ONE-CLICK INSTALLABILITY is the goal - a dependency would have been acceptable if it kept that, but none was needed.

VENDORED: engine/vendor/qrcode.ts remains from i8c, credited loudly in its header per the owner's ruling. Untouched here.

IMPORTED MODULES: kb is ABSENT on every grant this iteration recorded - the import stamp says so on all nine. That is the correct state after the junction incident, and se.law-imports-are-read-only governs any future re-attachment. No flip, no divergence.

EXTERNAL SERVICES, and these are the real dependencies of this iteration: (1) ntfy, already depended upon since i8, unchanged in kind - what changed is that we now speak its action protocol correctly; (2) NEW - Cloudflare Workers KV as the brief host. It is opt-in per machine, absent by default, and its absence costs only the third action. So the dependency is REAL but not LOAD-BEARING: the lane's floor - summon the owner, take the tap - depends on neither the store nor the network beyond ntfy itself. No sticky ruling was needed because the design document already ruled this transport at §18 and the owner had already provisioned the account; this iteration verified it live rather than deciding it.

DIVERGENCE: none. Nothing here forked or patched an upstream.

NO NEW ASK. The two decisions that would have needed the owner - whether to add a runtime dependency, and whether the store may hold evidence content - are already ruled: the first by the one-click ruling (moot, nothing added), the second by the accepted-risk model the owner set for the phone channel, now extended to brief content and tripwired as se.raid-brief-exports-evidence-content.
payload.upstream:
NONE OWED, and I checked rather than assumed.

Nothing upstream was patched, forked or worked around in this iteration. The two external protocols involved were used AS SPECIFIED and the failures were entirely ours: ntfy always required absolute http(s) action URLs and v1 already did it right - the bug was that v2 wrote a scheme-like token; Cloudflare KV behaved exactly as documented, and the only surprise was favourable (read-after-write measured at ~1s against the ~60s our own design document assumed, which corrects OUR folklore, not their behaviour).

The vendored qrcode library was not modified, so nothing is owed to it beyond the credit already in its header.

So: no proposal is deposited, because inventing one to fill this field would be noise. The corrections this iteration produced belong in OUR ledger - and they are there, as the absolute-URL ADR, the measured read-after-write figure, and the whitelist guards.
